label: copy-phase output of o/m/x/e/k, plus early y/0 inputs
explanation: Broad, weakly selective unit (active on 5% of steps). Two loosely related components. (1) Copy phase, about 65% of activation mass: fires when the token being output is o (rate 42%), m (32%), x (26%), e or k (17-18%), most often at recall_idx 2-4 and in short sequences (L=3-5). The strongest activations (up to 0.375) are copy steps outputting t/x/e/w right before an o is output (e.g. ...t o..., ...w e o...), but next_out==o alone is a weak predictor. (2) Original phase at t=0-1, when the input is y or 0 (in_tok y/0 rate ~19%), mostly at low-to-moderate magnitude. Almost silent in the middle and late original phase (orig_idx>=4) and at recall_idx 0-1. Even within the preferred output tokens most steps are inactive, so precision stays low (dev F1 0.43, mass recall 0.59); a lot of residual activation is spread over other tokens.
